Information since July points to a strengthening labor market and moderate real GDP growth. The pickup in business fixed investment is consistent with evidence that stronger internal funds and easier credit support capex (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994). With inflation below 2% but market- and survey-based expectations anchored, inflation-forecast targeting and New Keynesian frameworks (Svensson; Woodford; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans) support looking through hurricane-related, transitory price spikes while pursuing the symmetric 2% goal. Keeping the federal funds rate at 1–1¼% with guidance for gradual hikes, alongside initiating balance-sheet normalization, aligns with rule-like policy considerations (McCallum and Nelson, 1999) and VAR evidence (Sims; Zha) that measured tightening can sustain the expansion without unmooring expectations, a credibility reinforced by the Fed’s historical success in containing inflation (Volcker era) and commitment to avoid inflation bias (Romer).
